about: Assumptions for the 'Landed in India' estimate. Every number can be changed on the Cost calculator page; change the defaults here only with a new source.

freight_usd_kwh.note: China–India sea freight was about US$3,350–4,100 per 40ft container in October 2026 (indicative). Spread over roughly 4 MWh of 314 Ah cells per container this is about US$1/kWh; dangerous-goods (Class 9) surcharges and inland transport are not included, and heavy BESS containers often cost more to ship. Replace with your own quote.
freight_usd_kwh.source: Sino-Shipping, China to India freight guide (Oct 2026)

insurance_note: Indian customs takes 1.125% of FOB as notional insurance when the actual cost is not known.
insurance_source: EximPe: CIF, FOB and assessable value
bcd_note: 20% is the tariff rate for lithium-ion accumulators (8507 60 00); stationary BESS get a concessional 10%. The rate for cells imported to build EV packs depends on the exemption claimed and could not be confirmed from a public source, so the standard 20% is used.
duty_note: Assessable value = CIF (FOB + freight + insurance). Duty = BCD on assessable value, plus social welfare surcharge of 10% of BCD. IGST of 18% is charged on assessable value + BCD + SWS and is shown separately because businesses normally reclaim it.
duty_source: EximPe: CIF, FOB and assessable value
rebate_note: China removes its 6% export VAT rebate on batteries on 1 Jan 2027. The 'from 1 Jan' line assumes exporters raise prices by the full 6%.
fob_note: The China price (excluding VAT) stands in for the export (FOB) price. Real export quotes can differ by supplier, volume and terms.
